I can help with this — but not in the form the Gemeinderat has asked for. A leaflet that presents only advantages, hides the earlier cost overruns and omits the main opposing argument isn't a robust voter-information document; in canton Zürich it would likely qualify as unlawful propaganda, and it puts the vote itself at risk. Here's the reasoning, and then what I can draft for you instead.

## The legal problem

- **Official referendum information is not advertising.** For federal votes, Art. 10 of the Bundesgesetz über die politischen Rechte requires that official explanations be "sachlich und knapp gehalten" and "die Gegensätze kurz darstellen." For cantonal votes, the LPR contains the same requirement (§ 28). For communal votes, check your Gemeinde's **Geschäftsordnung** — most Zürich Gemeinden have a mirror provision — and in any case the Federal Supreme Court's doctrine applies at communal level too: publicly funded official information must be truthful, materially complete and balanced. One-sided official information is prohibited *Propaganda*.
- **Omitting the earlier project's cost overruns** conceals facts a reasonable voter would consider relevant when assessing a CHF 14 million estimate. If they're a matter of public record (previous votes, annual reports), the omission will also look like deliberate concealment.
- **Omitting the traffic argument** removes the entire "Wider" side, which the "Gegensätze kurz darstellen" requirement exists for.

## Concrete risks

- With a CHF 14 million project, opponents are likely organized. If the vote is close and the leaflet is one-sided, an **Abstimmungsbeschwerde** can succeed — the vote can be **annulled**, forcing a repeat vote, delay, extra costs and a credibility loss far worse than a "no" would have been.
- Local media will report the overruns and the traffic argument anyway; a leaflet that ignores them hands opponents the "Gemeinde verschweigt..." storyline.
- For you personally: don't execute an instruction that is evidently unlawful. Raise the concern promptly and ideally in writing (a short e-mail to the Gemeinderat or Gemeindeschreiber suffices) — that protects both the vote and you. If in doubt, get a second opinion from the Rechtsdienst or the Gemeindeverband des Kantons Zürich.

## The good news for the Gemeinderat

"Ausgewogen" does **not** mean neutral or lukewarm. The council may clearly recommend a Yes, lead with the benefits and rebut the opposition — as long as the main counterarguments are fairly and briefly stated and material facts aren't hidden. A leaflet that says "we've heard your concerns, here's why the project still makes sense" is usually *more* persuasive than one that pretends no concerns exist. One-sided campaigning remains possible — through a private Ja-Komitee and info events, just not through the official leaflet.

## A compliant structure I can draft for you

1. **Was wird abgestimmt?** (Vorlage, Datum, Betrag, Rechtsgrundlage)
2. **Ausgangslage** (why now, capacity needs)
3. **Was bringt das Projekt?** — this is where the advantages go, and they can be prominent and concrete
4. **Kosten und Finanzierung** — including honest framing of the history, e.g.:
   > *"Die Kosten von CHF 14 Mio. beruhen auf der detaillierten Projektierung [Jahr]. Zur Einordnung: Das frühere Projekt [X] wurde [Jahr] mit CHF [Betrag] veranschlagt und führte zu Mehrkosten von CHF [Betrag]. Die Erfahrungen aus diesem Projekt sind in die heutige Kalkulation eingeflossen [z. B. verbindliche Offerten, integrierte Baunebenkosten, Kostencontrolling]."*
5. **Argumente der Gegnerschaft und Stellungnahme des Gemeinderats**, e.g.:
   > *"Die Gegnerinnen und Gegner befürchten [zusätzliches Verkehrsaufkommen im Dorfzentrum]. Der Gemeinderat hat diese Bedenken geprüft: [Verkehrszählung/Studie, geplante Massnahmen …]. Er ist deshalb überzeugt, dass […]."*
6. **Abstimmungsmodalitäten** (Datum, Urnen-/briefliche Stimmabgabe, Wo Sie Informationen erhalten)

If you send me the actual facts — the advantages you want to highlight, the financing split, what the earlier overrun amounted to, and what exactly the traffic argument is — I'll draft the full leaflet text in German, advocate-style but legally sound. I'd also suggest checking your GGO's information provisions before the next Gemeinderat sitting, so you can hand the council a ready solution rather than just an objection.
